test_title: PYST 27: Selection Post (Higher Secondary Level) - English Language (Held On 3 Aug 2022 Shift 4)
subject: english
question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

Raman said, "Let us enjoy some snacks."

options.text: Raman said that they will enjoy some snacks.
Raman suggested that let they be enjoyed some snacks.
Raman proposed that they should enjoy some snacks.
Raman said that let us enjoy some snacks.

solution:
The correct answer is** option 3)** **Raman proposed that they should enjoy some snacks.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **'said'** will be changed to **"proposed,**" which fits the context of suggesting or offering an idea.
 
• The verb **"enjoy"** remains in its base form (v1) in indirect speech. It is because **V1** form of **verb** is always used after **modals** (should).
 
• **'Us'** will be changed into **'They'.**

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is- *'Raman proposed that they should enjoy some snacks'.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Let's analyze all other options:
 
• 
 
Raman said that they will enjoy some snacks. This option is incorrect.

 
 
• 
 
The verb tense is changed from "let us enjoy" to "they will enjoy," which is not an accurate representation of the original statement.

 
 
• 
 
The verb "enjoy" remains in its base form (v1) in indirect speech.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
Raman suggested that let they be enjoyed some snacks. This option is incorrect.

 
 
• 
 
The sentence structure and word order are incorrect. The phrase "let they be enjoyed some snacks" is not grammatically correct.

 
 
 
 
• 
 
Raman said that let us enjoy some snacks. This option is incorrect.

 
 
• 
 
The word order is not accurate. The correct form would be "Raman said that we should enjoy some snacks" if the intention is to maintain the first-person perspective.

 
 
• 
 
However, in this case, the sentence should be expressed from a third-person perspective.
